show.title: Creating Your Ladder
show.author: Stefano Di Rico
show.description:
Over the past five years, I’ve been able to do things I love: campaigning, working in start-ups, meeting incredibly inspiring individuals, alongside my studies. Trying lots of different things is how I found my reason to get up each morning and worked out what fulfils me.

If you don't know who I am: Hi, I'm Stefano. I've been a mental health campaigner for nearly six years, and along the way, I was able to find what fuelled me. Now, I'm on a mission to help other young people do the same.

episodes.title: Peter Wood on Creating Your Ladder | From feeling nothing at 14 to CEO at 25 | Graduate pathways are changing. Here's what to do instead | Personal brands for 2027 graduates | LinkedIn Top Voice.
episodes.description:
Is AI killing graduate jobs? Peter Wood has never made a CV, and at 25 he's CEO of a private equity-backed business. On this episode of Creating Your Ladder, Peter joins Stefano Di Rico to give his advice to young people developing their careers.

Despite a tough graduate jobs market, Peter remains optimistic. We talk about why the career ladder has turned into a climbing wall, the underemployment nobody talks about, why he never wrote a CV, the moment at 14 when he felt nothing at all, and how to get past the fear of cringe on LinkedIn. If you've ever felt stuck applying for the same jobs as everyone else, this one's for you.

About Peter

Peter Wood co-founded The Graduate Guide, an early-careers podcast and community that was acquired by Apprentify Group, and he now runs Calibr, which helps businesses build their people's capability alongside AI. He studied history, scouts early-stage founders for EWOR, and is launching a new media company about ambition.

In this episode

  • Why AI is taking the note-taker jobs, and where Peter still sees room for young people
  • Underemployment: capable graduates still applying for the same closing pathways
  • Why you can't build serendipity "behind a screen, applying to brand names that are probably sifting you out with AI"
  • The career ladder is now a climbing wall, and why working out what you don't like counts as experience
  • What got Peter through feeling "absolutely nothing" at 14
  • Who tells you that you need a personal brand, and how to post when you're scared of looking cringe.

episodes.title: Adam Raillard | How to network when you don’t know anyone | How to network when you don’t know anyone | Six looks in a month for London Fashion Week | Creating Your Ladder with Stefano Di Rico
episodes.description:
At 17, Adam Raillard sent 350 cold emails to get into London Fashion Week. A year later, he was presenting his own collection there.

Adam is the founder of streetwear brand The Kong Is Dead. With no sewing experience, a tiny pink sewing machine and YouTube tutorials, he made six looks in a month for his debut show, Minus One. We talk about how to break into fashion, why he walks straight up to the scariest person in the room, finding out he had ADHD at 17, and why he’d rather people love or hate his clothes than feel nothing. If you’ve ever wanted to break into an industry where you don’t know anyone, this one’s for you.

In this episode

  • How a spreadsheet and 350 cold emails turned into a backstage role at London Fashion Week
  • Why talking to the scariest person in the room first makes every other conversation easier
  • The difference between meeting 70 people in a night and actually building relationships
  • Going from backstage helper to presenting his own collection a year later
  • Growing up with undiagnosed ADHD, and why he chose not to take deadline extensions
  • Why goals change when you’re young, and why that’s normal

Adam Raillard is a designer and the founder of The Kong Is Dead, a streetwear brand he launched while studying at London College of Fashion. He presented his first collection, Minus One, at London Fashion Week in February 2026.

episodes.title: Alice Mazón | How to be taken seriously when you’re young | How Big Food targets teenagers | Volunteering in Calais at 18: a different type of gap year | Creating Your Ladder with Stefano Di Rico
episodes.description:
Alice Mazón has spent five years campaigning against Big Food, and she still finds walking into a school assembly terrifying. We talk about being dismissed at a conference because of her age, volunteering in Calais at 18, why McDonald's has become the youth club of today, and the two years she spent with a Nokia instead of a smartphone. If you've ever felt too young or too inexperienced to speak up, this one's for you.

In this episode

  • Why McDonald's has become the youth club of today, now that real youth clubs have closed
  • What happened when someone at a conference lost interest once they learnt her age, and her mum's reframe
  • Why she spent her gap year volunteering in Calais at 18, and how she handles the white saviour question
  • How Forced to Flee helps young people talk about migration without it turning into a row
  • Why she spent two years with a Nokia, and what it taught her about boundaries
  • Why everything is a lot more low-stakes than you think.

Alice co-directs Forced to Flee, an international NGO with 50 volunteers across 23 countries. She has campaigned with Bite Back for five years and studies Anthropology and Politics at the LSE.
